name: Dent Disease

criteria.description: Presence of low molecular weight proteinuria
Evidence of nephrocalcinosis or nephrolithiasis on imaging
Positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutations in CLCN5 or OCRL genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low molecular weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria, and nephrocalcinosis/nephrolithiasis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical criteria are met.

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease

rare.symptomName: Muscle weakness secondary to electrolyte imbalance

laboratory: Low molecular weight proteinuria (e.g., elevated β2-microglobulin or retinol-binding protein in urine)
Elevated serum creatinine in advanced disease
imaging: CT scan or X-ray demonstrating nephrolithiasis
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in CLCN5 gene (Dent disease type 1)
Pathogenic mutations in OCRL gene (Dent disease type 2)
other: Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction with glucosuria, aminoaciduria, and phosphaturia
Often caused by acquired conditions or other inherited disorders
Excessive oxalate production leading to recurrent kidney stones
Normal or low urinary calcium excretion

redFlags: Early onset nephrocalcinosis in a male patient
Persistent low molecular weight proteinuria despite normal glomerular function
Family history of kidney stones or renal failure with X-linked inheritance pattern
references: Wrong O, Norden AG, Feest TG, et al. Dent's disease: a familial proximal tubular nephropathy with low-molecular-weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive renal failure. Kidney Int. 1994;45(6):1600-1607.
Lloyd SE, Pearce SH, Fisher SE, et al. A common molecular basis for three inherited kidney stone diseases. Nature. 1996;379(6564):445-449.
